cross_case_findings: Multiple labels are justified when spans answer distinct reader questions; shared text or grammar alone does not establish a separate job.
Short partial definitions and declarative or cognitive instructions can be meaningful in context; completeness and imperative form are not universal prerequisites.
Distinguish the author’s claims and reported sources from verified truth; preserve hedges, speaker attribution, and the exact scope of qualifications.
A cited concrete study can both illustrate and support a claim, while an analogy can illustrate or compare without proving the proposition.
Anchors should include the specific relationship described in the reason; overly broad or partial anchors can conceal target and extraction errors.
Narrative, report and interpretation can overlap, but an enduring absence or isolated fact need not independently develop an event.
